name: Button Mash
description: Emulation guides and explainers (summaries; full text in data/guides.json).

guides.title: EmulatorJS self-hosting guide
guides.summary: Host the open-source EmulatorJS player on your own site and play ROMs you dumped yourself — setup, cores, BIOS, and the legal line.

guides.title: RetroArch setup guide
guides.summary: Install RetroArch, add cores for hardware you own, and load your own dumped games — controllers, save states, shaders, and netplay included.

guides.title: GBA-to-WASM recompiler guide
guides.summary: Turn a GBA cartridge you own into a self-contained browser page via static recompilation — the user-supplied-ROMs-only pattern, end to end.

guides.title: Rip-your-own-cartridges guide
guides.summary: Turn cartridges you own into verified ROM backups with a USB dumper — hardware picks, the dumping ritual, and the no-distribution rule.

guides.title: Homebrew & public-domain sources
guides.summary: Where to find legal homebrew ROMs and public-domain games: archives, dev communities, itch.io, and open-source originals.

guides.title: How GBA becomes WebAssembly
guides.summary: The reverse-engineering pattern behind browser GBA: ARM/THUMB basic blocks lifted into real WASM, frame timing, memory mapping — original explainer.

guides.title: How emulation works
guides.summary: Plain-English explainer: interpreters vs. recompilers, cycle accuracy, what a BIOS does, save states, and why the browser is enough now.

guides.title: Best emulator per system
guides.summary: One honest emulator pick per classic system: accuracy, ease of use, platform notes. Software only — no ROM links.

guides.title: Game Boy Advance emulation guide
guides.summary: The Player's gba core is mGBA (verified backend, the single GBA backend in the EmulatorJS core list). BIOS-free. Covers the settings that matter (color correction, fast-forward, Keep in Browser), save states/cheats wired to Player 2.0, a Player deep link (player.html?core=gba), and a curl-verified homebrew starter pack.

guides.title: SNES emulation guide
guides.summary: The Player's snes core is Snes9x (default SNES backend in the EmulatorJS core list; bsnes is the alternate for accuracy purists). BIOS-free. Covers hi-res blending, sound buffer/latency, save states and Game Genie/Pro Action Replay cheats via Player 2.0, deep link (player.html?core=snes), and a verified homebrew starter pack.

guides.title: NES emulation guide
guides.summary: The Player's nes core is FCEUmm (default NES backend in the EmulatorJS core list; Nestopia UE is the alternate for accuracy purists). BIOS-free for cartridges — the one exception is Famicom Disk System disks, which need a BIOS dumped from your own hardware. Covers mapper support, the sprite-flicker switch, save states and Game Genie cheats via Player 2.0, deep link (player.html?core=nes), and a verified homebrew starter pack.

guides.title: Nintendo 64 emulation guide
guides.summary: The Player's n64 core is Mupen64Plus-Next (default N64 backend in the EmulatorJS core list; alternate Parallel-N64). BIOS-free. Honest about per-game quirks and real hardware requirements: framebuffer emulation fixes most games, internal resolution is the performance lever, weak devices should pick SNES/GBA instead. Deep link (player.html?core=n64) and verified homebrew starter pack.

guides.title: PlayStation emulation guide
guides.summary: The Player's psx core is PCSX-ReARMed (default PSX backend in the EmulatorJS core list; alternate Mednafen PSX HW). BIOS honesty: boots via HLE with no BIOS, but a user-dumped scph BIOS improves accuracy (never download one). Covers enhanced resolution, fast-load, saves/cheats via Player 2.0, deep link (player.html?core=psx), and a verified homebrew starter pack.

guides.title: Genesis emulation guide
guides.summary: The Player's segaMD core is Genesis Plus GX (default Genesis/Game Gear/Sega CD backend in the EmulatorJS core list). BIOS-free (Sega CD aside). Covers region/6-button-pad/SRAM-autosave/audio-filter settings, saves and Game Genie cheats via Player 2.0, deep link (player.html?core=segaMD), and a verified homebrew starter pack.

guides.title: Game Boy / Color emulation guide
guides.summary: The Player's gb core is Gambatte (default GB backend in the EmulatorJS core list; alternate mGBA) — cycle-accurate, BIOS-free, and full speed on any device. Covers colorization palettes, saves and Game Genie/GameShark cheats via Player 2.0, deep link (player.html?core=gb), and a verified homebrew starter pack (GBDev community included).

guides.title: Make games for dead consoles: the homebrew development primer
guides.summary: Write your own games for the GBA, Game Boy, and NES: the honest toolchain (devkitARM, RGBDS, cc65), how to learn the hardware via Tonc and gbdev.io, testing on emulators and flash carts, and shipping through jams, itch.io, and showcases.

guides.title: Play together online: the netplay guide
guides.summary: Retro multiplayer over the internet: how RetroArch's rewind-based rollback netplay works, the same-version-same-core-same-game rule, hosting via lobby/relay/port-forward, what plays well (8/16-bit) and what doesn't (PS1/N64, link cables), plus Dolphin's 2026 Android netplay.

guides.title: Saves that survive: states, SRAM & backup workflows
guides.summary: Save states vs. battery saves vs. memory cards: what each one is, where it lives in RetroArch and in this site's Player (IndexedDB, Keep in Browser, named slots), moving saves between emulators, and the 3-2-1 backup routine.

guides.title: Make pixels look right: CRT shaders & display science
guides.summary: Why retro games look wrong on modern screens, the anatomy of the CRT look (scanlines, grille, glow), shader presets from zfast-crt to crt-royale, integer vs. bilinear scaling, and the honest science of input lag, run-ahead, and refresh rates.

guides.title: Retro games for every player: an accessibility guide
guides.summary: Old games shipped zero accessibility features — the emulator layer adds what they lack: remapping, turbo/autofire, rewind, save states, color correction, and honest difficulty options. No medical claims, just the toolbox.

guides.title: Keep your games forever: the preservation guide
guides.summary: Archive your own library properly: checksums (CRC32/SHA-1), No-Intro and Redump verification, the modern redumper/MPF/OmniDrive disc-dumping stack, lossless CHD compression, ROM managers and DAT files, and the 3-2-1 backup rule.

guides.title: Controllers in the browser: the gamepad setup guide
guides.summary: Get any USB or Bluetooth controller working with browser games and this site's Player — the Gamepad API, testing, per-system remapping, and honest troubleshooting.

guides.title: PICO-8 spotlight: the fantasy console's best corners
guides.summary: Meet the fantasy console with thousands of tiny games: Splore, the Lexaloffle BBS, where the gems hide, and how to play everything free in your browser.

guides.title: Cheat codes, decoded: Game Genie, GameShark & the Konami Code
guides.summary: Every cheat code is an address plus a value. Covers the two families (RAM codes vs ROM patches), the Konami Code's origin (Hashimoto, the 1986 NES Gradius port, Contra's 30 lives in 1988), the Game Genie (Codemasters/Galoob, 1990; six-letter codes patch unconditionally, eight-letter codes add a compare byte), the 1992 Ninth Circuit ruling in Lewis Galoob Toys v. Nintendo that made home cheat use fair use, GameShark/Action Replay (Datel hardware, InterAct's US brand from 1996), cheats in this site's Player (per-game codes via the Cheats tool, EJS_cheats, toggled in the in-game menu), finding your own codes with a RetroArch memory search, and where cheats don't belong (multiplayer, hardcore achievements). Legal lane: codes are numbers, never downloads.
